answer: Warm-up traffic-shape quota requires each new identity to show sparse, irregular requests across several observation windows before full-rate access. A timing ledge enforces it: synchronized bursts with no idle gaps keep quota at zero and discard the attempt. Each identity must also emit a low-rate keepalive beacon throughout warm-up. An attacker pays one live session per identity across real wall-clock windows, plus a failed-attempt nectar cost when bursts reset.
